entry.title: a raven in Anchorage, Alaska (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that a raven in Anchorage, Alaska (pictured), ate tater tots and toast, fought over ice cream, and disassembled a streetlamp?

entry.title: Wang Hanlun (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Wang Hanlun used proceeds from her company's only film to finalize her divorce?

entry.title: An American Overture (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Benjamin Britten wanted the score of his An American Overture destroyed after it was rediscovered?

entry.title: Dr Disrespect (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Dr Disrespect's first videos featured a bombastic "champion" trash-talking game-play footage?

entry.title: the second of which (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Cordova, Alabama, was hit by two tornadoes on the same day in 2011, the second of which was on the ground for more than two hours?

entry.title: Arthur France (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Arthur France founded the Leeds West Indian Carnival, the first Caribbean carnival in Europe, in 1967?

entry.title: published Tetris (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Spectrum HoloByte published Tetris without permission from the Soviet Union?

entry.title: 7th National Eucharistic Congress (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that a future World War II aircraft carrier was used as a hotel during the 7th National Eucharistic Congress in 1935?

entry.title: John Moore (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that John Moore's mother, after learning that UCLA's student-body president was Black, said "this is where he's going to school"?
